newsitem.title: UK: European VGO softens in talk after crude fell.
newsitem.headline: European VGO softens in talk after crude fell.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil prices weakened slightly by the end of the week on the back of falling crude futures, traders said.

They assessed low sulphur VGO cargoes around the $121/$123 fob level compared with $123/126 by mid-week but no fresh deals were heard done. The market was firm then on the back of a wide open trans-Atlantic arb and stronger European demand.

One Scandinavian refiner was offering on Thursday at $125 fob, but a trader said this level "was much too high at the moment". The refiner said that the buying interest vanished after oil futures fell in New York.
"VGO went bananas yesterday. I had bids at $125 but it all died away after NYMEX came down," the refiner said.
"It looks like a stalemate in the market at the moment with crude coming off. People are not prepared to talk about VGO awaiting to see if crude will come back up," one trader said.
However, avails were still seen low, which was keeping the levels from falling further.
Traders said they were waiting for the U.S. market to come back into action on Monday after Friday's July 4 holiday.
